snippet.textDisplay:
Logon ka criticize karna aajkal trend ban gaya hai, lekin ek flop se kisi superstar ka career define nahi hota. Salman Khan woh naam hai jinhone 30 saal se zyada Bollywood ko blockbuster films di hain – Hum Aapke Hain Koun, Bajrangi Bhaijaan, Sultan, Kick, Wanted, Dabangg series, Ek Tha Tiger, Tiger Zinda Hai jaise kai superhits.

Unhone naye actors ko launch kiya, dusron ki madad ki, aur apne charitable trust ‘Being Human’ ke zariye hazaaron zindagiyan behtar banayi hain. Har superstar ke career mein ups & downs aate hain – Shah Rukh ho ya Aamir – lekin yeh log sirf ek film se judge nahi kiye ja sakte. Sikandar chali ya nahi, lekin Salman Khan ka fanbase aur unka contribution kabhi kam nahi ho sakta. Respect dena seekhiye – criticism aur trolling mein fark hota hai.❤❤

snippet.textDisplay:
Every time a Salman Khan movie is announced, the excitement automatically kicks in.
The trailer looks promising and expectations rise… but after watching the film, the disappointment feels even worse than before.
It has become a never-ending cycle —
good trailer → huge hype → weak storyline → regret.
Sometimes it makes you wonder: would any sensible actor even sign such scripts?
But then again, Salman Khan doesn’t risk his own money. He knows that even a bad film will cross ₹200+ crore because of his massive fan base. So where is the pressure to improve?
The real question is —
does Salman Khan still want to work with strong storytellers and visionary directors like Prashanth Neel, S.S. Rajamouli, or Sandeep Reddy Vanga?
Or are these directors simply not interested anymore?
Instead, we keep getting films with directors whose past work already tells us what to expect.
Just seeing their names is enough to predict the final result.
If Battle of Girlban turns out to be another disaster, it won’t really matter.
Another bigger disaster will follow.
The producer will recover the money.
The star will move on.
Only the audience will be left disappointed — again.
Still, fans will show up.
So yes…
Get ready for Battle of Girlban.
हिंदी
हर बार जब सलमान ख़ान की कोई नई फ़िल्म अनाउंस होती है, तो अपने आप एक एक्साइटमेंट आ जाती है।
ट्रेलर अच्छा लगता है, उम्मीदें बढ़ जाती हैं… लेकिन फ़िल्म देखने के बाद हर बार निराशा और भी ज़्यादा बढ़ जाती है।
यह एक अंतहीन चक्र बन चुका है —
अच्छा ट्रेलर → ज़बरदस्त हाइप → कमज़ोर कहानी → पछतावा।
कभी-कभी मन में सवाल आता है —
क्या ऐसी स्क्रिप्ट पर कोई समझदार एक्टर साइन भी करता?
लेकिन फिर याद आता है कि सलमान ख़ान अपनी जेब से पैसा नहीं लगाते। उन्हें पता है कि उनकी फ़िल्म चाहे जैसी भी हो, उनका फैनबेस उसे 200 करोड़ के पार पहुँचा ही देगा। तो फिर सुधार करने की ज़रूरत ही कहाँ है?
असली सवाल यह है —
क्या सलमान ख़ान अब भी प्रशांत नील, एस.एस. राजामौली या संदीप रेड्डी वांगा जैसे दमदार डायरेक्टर्स के साथ काम करना चाहते हैं?
या फिर ऐसे डायरेक्टर्स उनके साथ काम करने में दिलचस्पी ही नहीं रखते?
इसके बजाय, बार-बार उन्हीं डायरेक्टर्स के साथ फ़िल्में बन रही हैं जिनका पिछला काम देखकर ही आगे का अंदाज़ा लग जाता है।
उनके नाम से ही फ़िल्म का हाल समझ आ जाता है।
अगर Battle of Girlban भी एक और डिज़ास्टर निकलती है, तो शायद किसी को ज़्यादा फर्क नहीं पड़ेगा।
इसके बाद उससे भी बड़ा डिज़ास्टर आएगा।
प्रोड्यूसर अपना पैसा निकाल लेगा।
स्टार आगे बढ़ जाएगा।
और दर्शक… फिर से निराश होंगे।
फिर भी, लोग फ़िल्म देखने जाएँगे।
तो हाँ —
Battle of Girlban के लिए तैयार रहिए।

snippet.textDisplay: Honestly, this movie was pretty bad—the dialogues were laughable. Salman just doesn’t seem agile anymore; his posture looks awkward, and it feels like he’s lost that spark he once had. I think it might be time for him to focus on his health instead of acting. The fun, lively Salman I used to enjoy is long gone—now his acting feels stiff and forced. I’m not trying to hate, but pairing him with actresses young enough to be his granddaughter is just odd. Most of the positive reviews seem to come from die-hard fans or maybe even paid promotions. Trust me, you’ll probably regret watching this movie within the first 30 minutes.

snippet.textDisplay:
Sikandar is an unmitigated debacle, proof that even Salman Khan’s brio can’t redeem a floundering fiasco. It opens with Bhai sauntering in, his inimitable panache briefly perspicuous, but the film plummets into a 2.5-hour morass of execrable writing and risible acting. A.R. Murugadoss, once the architect of Ghajini’s visceral clarity and Thuppakki’s cerebral verve, delivers a tenebrous mess—where’s the incisive pacing, the poignant wallop? This is a cacophonous relic, saddled with overwrought action and a lugubrious organ-donor thread that’s dead on arrival.

The performances? Abysmal. Salman’s ossified in rote—flailing fists and barking lines like a jaded leviathan, bereft of nuance, all bluster. Rashmika Mandanna’s a cipher, her chemistry with Khan nonexistent, her demise so vapid you’d rather peruse X than mourn. Prateik Babbar and Sathyaraj ham it up with histrionics fit for a provincial pantomime—snarling sans gravitas. Even Sharman Joshi, a lone scintilla, can’t salvage this dreck. Against Ghajini’s Aamir or Thuppakki’s Vijay, this troupe seems to grope through a thespian void. 2/5 stars—eschew it unless you’re an obdurate Salman acolyte.
